entities.name: Telesphorus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pope Telesphorus was the bishop of Rome from c. 126 to his death in 137 CE, during the reigns of Roman Emperors Hadrian and Antoninus Pius.

This pope played a crucial role in navigating the complexities of the Roman Empire's declining power and the rise of Christianity as a major world religion.

His papacy was marked by significant theological debates with the Donatists, a Christian sect that emerged during the 4th century CE.

The Donatist controversy led to the Second Council of Carthage in 417 CE, where Telesphorus was present and played a key role in resolving the conflict.

Despite his efforts, the legacy of Telesphorus remains somewhat overshadowed by that of his more famous successors, Pope Gregory I and Pope Innocent III.

A striking testament to the enduring influence of Telesphorus lies in the fact that he was revered as a saint by the Catholic Church by the 7th century CE, a recognition that underscores the lasting impact of his leadership.
